provenance.note: Practice questions for Aga Khan University (AKU) Medical College admission test. Science Achievement section covering Biology, Chemistry, and Physics at intermediate/Higher Secondary level. Not affiliated with AKU.

marking.note: 50 MCQs, no negative marking (AKU admission test pattern).

questions.stem: Which organelle is responsible for the synthesis of proteins in a cell?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the cellular organelles that synthesise proteins by translating messenger RNA.

questions.stem: Which part of the cell controls all its activities and contains the genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell and houses the chromosomes carrying genetic material (DNA).

questions.stem: Which type of blood cells primarily defends the body against infection?
questions.explanation: White blood cells (leucocytes) fight infections by engulfing pathogens and producing antibodies.

questions.stem: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the cell's ATP through cellular respiration, earning them the name powerhouse of the cell.

questions.stem: Which gas is released as a by-product of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: During photosynthesis plants convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and release oxygen as a by-product.

questions.stem: What is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms?
questions.explanation: The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out all the processes of life; tissues, organs and systems are built from cells.

questions.stem: Which organ of the human body pumps blood through the circulatory system?
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscular organ that contracts rhythmically to pump blood around the body.

questions.stem: The green pigment in plant leaves that absorbs light energy for photosynthesis is:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green photosynthetic pigment found in chloroplasts that absorbs light energy.

questions.stem: How many chromosomes are present in a normal human somatic (body) cell?
questions.explanation: Human somatic cells are diploid and contain 46 chromosomes (23 pairs); gametes contain only 23.

questions.stem: Which organelle is mainly involved in the synthesis of lipids and the detoxification of drugs in the liver?
questions.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum lacks ribosomes and is the site of lipid synthesis and drug detoxification.

questions.stem: Which hormone, secreted by the pancreas, lowers the level of glucose in the blood?
questions.explanation: Insulin, released by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans, promotes glucose uptake and lowers blood glucose.

questions.stem: In human lungs, the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place across the walls of the:
questions.explanation: The alveoli are thin-walled air sacs surrounded by capillaries where gaseous exchange occurs.

questions.stem: The enzyme present in human saliva that begins the digestion of starch is:
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) hydrolyses starch into maltose in the mouth.

questions.stem: DNA replication is described as semiconservative because:
options: Each new DNA molecule contains one parental and one newly synthesised strand
Both strands of the new molecule are entirely new
DNA is copied from an RNA template
Replication occurs only in prokaryotic cells
questions.explanation: In semiconservative replication each daughter molecule keeps one original strand and one new complementary strand, as shown by the Meselson-Stahl experiment.

questions.stem: Which type of cell division produces four haploid daughter cells from one diploid parent cell?
questions.explanation: Meiosis involves two successive divisions and halves the chromosome number, producing four haploid gametes.

questions.stem: The part of the human brain that maintains balance and coordinates voluntary movement is the:
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates muscle movements and maintains posture and balance.

questions.stem: In a DNA double helix, adenine always pairs with:
questions.explanation: Complementary base pairing in DNA is A-T and G-C, held together by hydrogen bonds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is considered a vestigial organ in humans?
questions.explanation: The vermiform appendix has lost most of its original digestive function in humans and is a vestigial structure.

questions.stem: Which organelle contains hydrolytic enzymes that digest worn-out organelles and foreign material?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs of hydrolytic enzymes that carry out intracellular digestion.

questions.stem: The theory of evolution through natural selection was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species (1859) proposed natural selection as the mechanism of evolution.

questions.stem: Which functional group is characteristic of alcohols?
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl functional group (-OH) attached to a saturated carbon atom.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol of sodium?
questions.explanation: Sodium's symbol Na comes from its Latin name natrium.

questions.stem: The pH of a neutral solution at 25°C is:
questions.explanation: At 25°C a neutral solution has pH 7, where [H+] = [OH-] = 10^-7 mol/dm^3.

questions.stem: Which gas is commonly known as laughing gas?
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is called laughing gas because of its euphoric effect when inhaled.

questions.stem: The chemical formula of methane is:
questions.explanation: Methane, the simplest hydrocarbon of the alkane family, has the formula CH4.

questions.stem: Which state of matter has both a definite shape and a definite volume?
questions.explanation: Solids have fixed shape and volume because their particles are tightly packed in a regular arrangement.

questions.stem: Which element has the highest electronegativity in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Fluorine (3.98 on the Pauling scale) is the most electronegative element.

questions.stem: According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing the temperature of an exothermic reaction at equilibrium will:
options: Shift the equilibrium towards the reactants
Shift the equilibrium towards the products
questions.explanation: Raising the temperature favours the endothermic (reverse) direction, so an exothermic equilibrium shifts towards the reactants.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the simplest alkene?
questions.explanation: Ethene (C2H4) is the simplest alkene, containing one carbon-carbon double bond.

questions.stem: The rate of a chemical reaction generally ___ as the temperature is increased.
questions.explanation: Higher temperature increases the kinetic energy of molecules, raising the frequency and energy of effective collisions and hence the reaction rate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Argon belongs to Group 18; noble gases have completely filled valence shells and are chemically inert.

questions.stem: Which reagent is commonly used in the laboratory to test for unsaturation in organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Bromine water is decolourised by alkenes and alkynes, confirming the presence of multiple bonds.

questions.stem: For a first-order reaction, the half-life is:
options: Directly proportional to the initial concentration
Inversely proportional to the initial concentration
questions.explanation: For first-order kinetics t1/2 = 0.693/k, which does not depend on the initial concentration.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds can show geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism?
questions.explanation: 2-butene has a carbon-carbon double bond with different groups on each carbon, allowing cis and trans forms.

questions.stem: In a coordination compound, a ligand donates a lone pair of electrons to the central metal ion, forming a:
questions.explanation: A coordinate (dative covalent) bond forms when one species provides both electrons of the shared pair.

questions.stem: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N); 1 N = 1 kg m/s^2.

questions.stem: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes (A), defined as one coulomb of charge per second.

questions.stem: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately:
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 3 × 10^8 m/s (300,000 km/s) in vacuum.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector; speed, mass and temperature are scalars.

questions.stem: Which law states that the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it at constant temperature?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law states V = IR; the current is directly proportional to voltage when resistance is constant.

questions.stem: The smallest particle of an element that retains the chemical properties of the element is the:
questions.explanation: The atom is the smallest unit of an element that takes part in chemical reactions and retains its identity.

questions.stem: According to Newton's second law of motion, the net force acting on a body equals:
questions.explanation: Newton's second law states F = ma; force equals the product of mass and acceleration.

questions.stem: The photoelectric effect was explained by Albert Einstein in 1905 using:
questions.explanation: Einstein proposed that light consists of quanta (photons), each carrying energy E = hf, explaining the photoelectric effect.

questions.stem: Two resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance of the combination?
questions.explanation: In a series circuit resistances add: 4 + 6 = 10 Ω.

questions.stem: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of:
questions.explanation: The atomic number (Z) is the number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the identity of the element.

questions.stem: The kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with velocity v is given by:
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy K = 1/2 mv^2; it depends on the square of the velocity.

questions.stem: The magnetic effect of an electric current (deflection of a compass needle near a current-carrying wire) was discovered by:
questions.explanation: In 1820 Ørsted observed that a current-carrying wire deflects a magnetic needle, revealing the magnetic effect of current.

questions.stem: Total internal reflection of light is the principle underlying the working of:
questions.explanation: Optical fibres guide light through repeated total internal reflection along the core-cladding boundary.

questions.stem: In an ideal transformer, the relationship between primary voltage Vp, secondary voltage Vs and the number of turns Np and Ns is:
questions.explanation: The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio: Vp/Vs = Np/Ns.

questions.stem: A car moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest uniformly in 5 seconds. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: a = (v - u)/t = (0 - 20)/5 = -4 m/s^2; the negative sign shows deceleration.
